title: Why You Should Be Looking for Benzo Detox Facilities
h1: Why You Should Be Looking for Benzo Detox Facilities
metaDescription: If you are addicted to prescription drugs, you may need to detox before recovery. Read how to find benzo detox facilities and get help now.

blocks.text: It is common for individuals struggling with anxiety, panic disorders, and other physical and psychological conditions to be prescribed medication to deal with their symptoms. But what happens when this medication becomes addictive? Even if you begin the use of prescription drugs with the best intentions, it can be hard to stop taking them and it can begin to interfere with your day-to-day life. Marina Harbor Detox provides a safe destination for those struggling with addiction or withdrawal related to benzos and other prescription drugs. If you or a loved one is searching for a way to overcome an addiction, a benzo detox facility may be the answer.

Benzos, or benzodiazepines, are a class of psychoactive drugs that act on specific receptors in the brain to produce calming effects. Benzodiazepines can be used to treat a number of medical conditions including anxiety, panic disorders, and seizures, and can be used as a muscle relaxant or to treat alcohol withdrawal symptoms. There are several different benzodiazepines on the market, which vary based on how quickly they start working, how long they work for, and what ailments they have been prescribed for. Some of the most common benzos that are commonly prescribed include diazepam (Valium), alprazolam (Xanax), lorazepam (Ativan), and clonazepam (Klonopin). Even though benzos are designed to have a calming effect, they are also highly addictive and are often associated with substance use disorders. The withdrawal effects upon beginning a detox from benzos can be extremely severe and even life-threatening. Benzos also come with a high risk of potential overdosing.

If you or a loved one is struggling with an addiction to benzodiazepines, it’s important to remember that help is available to you. Entering a drug detox facility is recommended for those going through withdrawal resulting from a drug addiction. Benzo detox facilities are essential due to the high risk of severe withdrawal symptoms. In these facilities, specialized medical professionals provide supervision around the clock to ensure the safety of each individual. Therapists and counselors are also on hand to provide individual and group therapy, addressing the emotional and psychological effects of detoxing.
Why You Should Never Detox from Benzos at Home

Due to the tolerance that is built up over time during a benzodiazepine addiction, dangerous withdrawal symptoms will emerge upon beginning a detox from benzos. Benzo withdrawals can be incredibly dangerous, even putting those detoxing at risk for severe medical complications or even death. Detoxing should never be done without the oversight of a medical professional in a benzo detox facility to ensure a safe withdrawal period and a safe detoxification process.

Medical detox from benzos is designed to help reduce the effects of withdrawal symptoms and allows the body to completely eliminate the substance more safely and comfortably. During the withdrawal process, your treatment team will be able to assess and address any pain, anxiety, and physical and emotional symptoms of withdrawal you may be experiencing. While detoxing from benzos can be uncomfortable and scary, doing so in a monitored environment ensures your complete safety and comfort while beginning your journey toward overcoming your addiction.
